| [THEORY-028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md) v2 | The expected bias of any data-dependent choice, and the expected generalisation error of any learning algorithm, is at most √(2σ²·I) for σ-subgaussian losses, where I is the information the output carries about the data | Russo & Zou (2015), [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md), Prop. 1: \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) for any selection T among σ-sub-Gaussian statistics. | [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v2 | Landauer's principle prices only logically irreversible steps, and prices them in exported entropy rather than heat, so acquiring, copying or evaluating a bit, and learning it, carry no minimum thermodynamic cost | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state (erasure, merging of control flow), and it is at least k ln 2 of entropy exported per bit, which "need not" be heat. Information learnt is bounded by entropy production and can be paid almost entirely in weight entropy. The only per-bit heat term is Landauer's, on entropy removed. The synthesis across the three is the record's. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) | The likelihood-ratio detector is optimal under the payoff, Neyman–Pearson and posterior criteria, which differ only in its threshold, so performance is an ROC and the criterion a point on it; d′ is criterion-free only for equal-variance normal signal and noise | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). | [THEORY-262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-262.md) | Neural complexity is low when a system's parts are independent or uniformly dependent and high when small subsets are nearly independent while large ones are integrated; in simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity raises it above random connectivity of equal density | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman (1994), [LIT-998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-998.md), read in [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md). C_N, the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear rise with subset size, is shown low at both extremes for one family of Gaussian matrices, and higher for patchy than for uniform wiring in one simulated visual area and in small linear systems. All of it is simulation. It is a whole-system number over fixed components: it does not find units or boundaries. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-263.md) | A coding rate that varies with the realised sample and output makes rate-distortion generalisation bounds data-dependent, and with the rate set to the pointwise information density log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) against a fixed prior the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023; IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 2024), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). Theorem 1: with a sample-dependent rate R_{S,W}, gen ≤ √(4σ²(R_{S,W} + log(√(2n)/δ))/(2n−1) + ε). With R_{S,W} = log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) the coding condition holds at ε = 0 and the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. The general Theorems 3–5 recover Rivasplata et al.'s PAC-Bayes bound and Xu–Raginsky's. The coding construction is proved for finite alphabets only. The general proofs are change of measure. The rate is a Shannon code-length difference against a prior, not Kolmogorov complexity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-266.md) | The average generalisation error along an optimisation trajectory is bounded by the rate-distortion function of the trajectory's law given the sample, plus a coupling term that carries the trajectory's dependence on the sample | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), Theorem 7, read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). For an L-Lipschitz loss in [0, 1], with probability ≥ 1 − δ, the mean of gen(S, W^t) over iterations is at most √((RD(S, ε; π_S) + log(√(2n)M/δ))/(2n − 1) + 4Lε). RD is computed for the sample at hand. The coupling coefficient M depends on the unknown distribution and absorbs I(W^T; S). The CIFAR-10 experiment drops M and 4Lε and shows only that the estimated rate and the test gap fall together over learning rates. For FCN4 the plotted rate term is about 3, which is vacuous for 0–1 loss. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-268.md) | An emergence measure averaged over a system's transitions can be positive while its local value is negative at particular transitions, so emergence so measured belongs to the ensemble, not to each moment | Varley (2022), [LIT-953](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-953.md), read in full in [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md). Both the coarse-graining and the ΦID accounts of emergence score an expected past–future mutual information, whose pointwise values can be negative. In one constructed toy, about 53% of informative micro transitions map to misinformative macro ones, and the synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of transitions, while both averages are positive. The paper argues the possibility is general and shows it in instances; it does not show that every system flickers, or say what a negative moment means. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) | Translation without parallel data is learnable from a plausibility prior over the target language alone, with error falling in the common ground between prior and translations, in the size of the source language and in the number of samples | Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md). Proved for maximum likelihood in stylised random models with uniform languages and one-to-one translators; in one model the bound O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))) is tight up to a constant. Information- theoretic only. The prior substitutes for parallel data in learning the decoder, not for information in a message. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) v2 | Directional information measures between two symmetrically coupled units follow the path of a recorded drive, not the symmetry of the coupling: flow reads two-way under moderate drive of one unit and one-way under strong drive | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). Two colloids are coupled by the fluid through a symmetric tensor, and recorded noise moves one trap. Time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy give drive → driven → other, with backflow at moderate drive. In numerics only, flow is one-way at strong drive. With no drive the coupled particles are independent at steady state. The paper does not test an unrecorded drive shared by both units, and it does not claim that the measures reveal coupling architecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) | For individual data, at every bound on model complexity, the model with the shortest two-part code is, to within O(log n), the best-fitting model in randomness deficiency, although the fit itself cannot be computed or approximated | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) | Perfect concept erasure caps what a representation can keep at the information not about the concept: if Z is independent of A then I(Z;X) is at most H(X\|A), and a deterministic erasure reaches that cap only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another | Chowdhury et al. (2025), [LIT-963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-963.md), read in full in [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md). The cap (Lemma 3.3) is a two-line chain-rule argument that needs only the Markov condition A → X → Z. The permutation condition is proved necessary and sufficient for deterministic maps (Appendices A.3 and A.4), with finite supports and disjoint groups. The paper's further statement, that the cap cannot be reached when the groups are not permutations, is false for stochastic maps, which reach it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md) | For an optimal capacity-bounded learner on a mixture of equally frequent random facts and a second domain, the facts are learned not at all below a capacity threshold set by the mixing ratio and in full above it, and Pythia models trained on such mixtures show the same threshold in model size and in mixing ratio | Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md). Proved for an idealised learner whose capacity is mutual information with the data (Theorem 4.3), on an orthogonal mixture of uniform facts and a second domain; seen in Pythia models from 14M to 6.9B on synthetic biographies mixed into web text. The theory is static. It does not say when in training the facts arrive, and it does not show that SGD reaches the optimal allocation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md) v2 | The neural Donsker–Varadhan estimator of mutual information is strongly consistent as an extremum estimator over compact families of critics, and, for critics bounded by M and L-Lipschitz in their d parameters, its uniform deviation from the population bound needs a number of samples set by d, M, L and the parameter radius, not by the data dimension | Belghazi et al. (2018), [LIT-256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-256.md), §3.3 and App. 8.2.2–8.2.3, read in [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md). On a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, the supremum of the Donsker–Varadhan bound over some compact network family is within any η of the mutual information, and the empirical supremum converges to the population one almost surely. Uniform deviation ε needs Õ(d log d/ε²) samples for d parameters, under bounded, Lipschitz critics. The guarantee is for the exact empirical maximizer, not for gradient training. The finite-sample estimate is not a bound (Poole et al., [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md)), and the proof has two gaps a reading found. | Active |
| [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) | With a kernel normalised to k(x,x) = 1, the covariance operator of a distribution is a density operator, and its quantum relative entropy is a lower bound on the Kullback–Leibler divergence that is tight only for an orthonormal, hence discrete, embedding, lies above the KL of the kernel-smoothed distributions, and on the torus is within O(σ²) of KL as the bandwidth σ shrinks | Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md). Σ_p = ∫ϕϕ* dp is uncentred and unit-trace, so p ↦ Σ_p maps distributions to quantum states, and D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q) (Proposition 4(d), Eq. 8). The upper bound is joint convexity, with equality only if k(x,y) = 0 for x ≠ y. The lower bound is monotonicity under a measurement whose outcome law is p smoothed by h(x,y) = ⟨ϕ(x), Σ^{−1/2}ϕ(y)⟩². The O(σ²) gap is shown only for translation-invariant kernels on the torus with Lipschitz densities. It does not cover centred kernels, or similarity measures that compare Gram matrices of representations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-352](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-352.md) | A pseudorandom generator exists if and only if a one-way function exists, where both are secure against uniform adversaries and every reduction is an oracle Turing machine, as statements about ensembles indexed by n; the construction from an arbitrary one-way function is only weak-preserving, so security at one length is bought at a much greater one | Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md), with Goldreich's Foundations of Cryptography, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), skimmed in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) from the 1995 draft. Theorem 6.2.2: "There are one-way functions iff there are pseudorandom generators." The hard direction runs one-way function → false entropy generator → pseudoentropy generator → generator, by uniform reductions, with seeds of length n^10 in the direct construction. Adversaries are algorithms; the paper has no circuit version, and that the proof carries over to non-uniform adversaries is the reading's inference, not the paper's statement. Everything is asymptotic. Goldreich states the theorem and does not prove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md) | Computational indistinguishability is strictly coarser than statistical closeness: without any assumption there are ensembles on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform, though none of them is efficiently samplable, and an efficiently samplable pair of this kind exists if a pseudorandom generator does, since its output covers at most 2^n of the 2^l(n) strings; all of it is about ensembles indexed by n, not single pairs of distributions | Goldreich, Foundations of Cryptography vol. 1, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), read in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) (Skimmed, 1995 draft, Chapters 1–3 in full), with Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md). Proposition 3.3 proves by counting that some ensemble far from uniform fools every small circuit; its proof is non-constructive and the ensemble cannot be sampled efficiently. A generator's output is efficiently samplable, indistinguishable from uniform by definition, and statistically far by an image count (§3.3.1). That a samplable such pair exists only if one-way functions do is cited to Goldreich 1990, not read. The book's statistical difference has no factor ½, so it is twice total variation. | Active |
| [THEORY-399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md) | Storing every inner product of n points of the unit ball of R^k to additive error ε takes Θ(n log n/ε²) bits once k ≥ log n/ε² and Θ(nk log(2 + log n/(ε²k))) below, for 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, and comparing these counts across dimensions shows that some n such points cannot be mapped into fewer than Ω(min{k, log(2 + ε²n)/ε²}) dimensions with additive error ε for every ε ≥ 2/√n; this is a worst-case lower bound with unstated constants, the small-ε bit count is open for k above that dimension, and no one-family embedding that small is proved | Alon and Klartag (2017), [LIT-1151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md), read in [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) from arXiv v4. Theorem 1.1 gives the bits of an additive ε-distance sketch for every k when 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, by a volume argument above and a packing of net points against random probes below. Since an embedding is a sketch, Corollary 2.1 re-proves Larsen and Nelson's bound in that range, and Corollary 2.3, using the Gaussian correlation inequality in place of a union bound, extends it to every ε ≥ 2/√n with log(2 + ε²n) in place of log n. The dimension statements are for additive error on squared distances of points of norm at most 1; the relative form for small ε follows but is not stated. The matching upper bound for one set is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-404](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-404.md) | With a common prior, a sender who commits to a signal the receiver observes can induce any distribution of posteriors whose mean is the prior, so an openly designed experiment moves a fully informed Bayesian receiver whenever the concave closure of the sender's value lies above its value at the prior; at the optimum, under the paper's tie-breaking, the receiver is certain when she takes the sender's worst action and indifferent when she takes another | Kamenica & Gentzkow (2011), [LIT-1021](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1021.md), read in [NOTE-717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-717.md) with the proofs. Proved results (Proposition 1, Corollary 2, Propositions 4 and 5) for a single ideal Bayesian receiver, a finite state space, commitment and sender-preferred tie-breaking. A judge who knows the investigation was designed to convict convicts 60 percent of defendants when 70 percent are innocent. The paper does not analyse manipulation, does not compute the receiver's welfare and does not cite Blackwell. | Active |
| [THEORY-416](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-416.md) | Quantum thermodynamics has at least four inequivalent notions of work, the ensemble average, the two-point-measurement random variable, the ε-deterministic single-shot work content and the resource-theory work, which answer different operational questions; only the two single-shot optima coincide, by identification of formulas and for energy-diagonal states | Vinjanampathy & Anders (2015/16), [LIT-010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-010.md), read in full in [NOTE-011](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-011.md). The review's one synthesis (§5.2, §7) sets four definitions side by side: ⟨W⟩ = ∫tr[ρḢ]dt (Eq. 2), W = E_m^(τ) − E_n^(0) (Eq. 24), A^ε ≈ −kT ln(Z_Λ*/Z) (Eq. 49) and w^max_ε = F^min_ε(ρ_S) − F(τ_S) (Eq. 50). Only the last two agree, and that agreement is an observation that two published formulas match, for states diagonal in energy. It is an informed judgement of a 2016 snapshot, not a theorem that the notions cannot be unified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-424](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-424.md) | Mutual-information measures of individuality that read a system's next state off its present one measure association, not propagation: I(S_{t+1}; S_t) can be positive when the environment alone drives the system, and conditioning on the environment does not recover the interventional quantity, which can be zero where the conditional measure is one bit | Bourrat (2024), [LIT-005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), read in [NOTE-027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-027.md), against Krakauer et al.'s (2020) measures. A* = I(S_{t+1}; S_t) is confounded when the environment is a common cause (his Fig. 2), and his interventional Â = I(S_{t+1}; Ŝ_t) is zero there. His claim that Â equals Krakauer's conditional A = I(S_{t+1}; S_t \| E_t) is false in general: [NOTE-027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-027.md)'s XOR system has A = 1 bit and Â = 0. Â itself depends on an intervention distribution the paper leaves open, and neither it nor the paper's two ETI criteria is computed on any system. | Active |
| [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) | Evaluating expected free energy recursively over the beliefs an agent would hold after each plausible outcome makes active inference a pruned tree search over belief states, formally analogous to Bellman recursion, which lets the agent plan through short-term costs that one-step agents cannot; that the pruning keeps deep search tractable beyond toy problems is argued, not shown | Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp & Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), read in [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) as prose: the equations were not recoverable from the text layer. The recursion is a construction (strong). That it plans through costs rests on single deterministic runs of a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze. [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) declined a THEORY because the results are a construction plus illustrations; this one is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, stating only the claim the reading supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-479](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-479.md) | Shannon's chain rule is the 1-cocycle equation of a cohomology of finite probability spaces whose action is averaged conditioning, and on connected, sufficiently rich structures of partitions every measurable 1-cocycle is a constant multiple of Shannon entropy, with no symmetry or continuity axiom assumed; in the unitary-invariant quantum version the first cohomology vanishes and von Neumann entropy is the 0-cochain whose coboundary is minus Shannon entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md), read in [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md). Theorems 1 and 3 are proved for finite spaces, through the Tverberg–Kendall–Lee result on measurable solutions of the fundamental equation of information. The hypotheses are stated three different ways in the paper; Theorem 1's is operative. The higher mutual informations appear as coboundaries, and Theorems B, D and F and the synergy reading are sketched or deferred to companion papers, so they are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-497.md) v2 | A macro feature can supervene on a system's present state and still carry information about its future that no small set of parts carries, because supervenience is instantaneous and prediction runs across time; on the integrated-information-decomposition account a system can host such a feature of order k exactly when its dynamics carry k-th-order synergy about their own future, relative to a fixed partition into parts and a chosen redundancy function | Mediano et al. (2022), [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md), read in [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md), a review of Rosas et al. (2020), which the record does not hold. A feature V_t is causally emergent of order k iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0, and a system has one iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0, split as downward causation plus causal decoupling. The review proves none of this and names no redundancy function. The quantities change with the partition, which the review calls intended, and they are predictive, not interventional, unless p(X′ \| X) is a do()-distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-513](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-513.md) | Observational entropy taken relative to a maximum-entropy prior τ, S(τ) − D_M(ρ‖τ), lies between S(ρ) and S(τ) for states meeting the prior's constraint, is finite and continuous whenever S(τ) is, and reduces to about two dozen textbook entropies by choice of measurement and prior; its second laws are bounds on the time-averaged state's divergence from the prior, proved small only under sufficient conditions (nondegenerate energy gaps for equilibration, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis for fit to the prior) | Schindler, Strasberg, Galke, Winter & Jabbour (2025), [LIT-082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-082.md), read in full in [NOTE-043](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-043.md), with Proofs 1, 2, 7, 10 and 11 checked line by line. The bounds, the special cases and the decomposition are proved. The central target, a small divergence of the time-averaged state from the prior, is proved for no concrete system; in the paper's own examples "in none of those cases was the smallness proved here analytically" (p. 12). Unpublished as of the reading. | Active |
| [THEORY-523](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-523.md) | IIT 4.0's measure of integrated information is undefined for any system that has a non-Markovian graining, which brains are said to have under the grainings in use, and it has never been computed for a real physical system; so empirical measures such as PCI are proxies for it, not approximations, and their success is evidence for IIT's intuitions about integration, not for Φ | Barrett, Milinkovic, Mediano, Rosas, Bor, Barnett & Seth (2026), [LIT-185](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md), read in full in [NOTE-122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-122.md). A position paper by sympathetic insiders, with no new formal result. The ill-definedness is restated from Barrett & Mediano (2019), which the record does not hold. That brains are non-Markovian under typical grainings rests on one 1998 citation about ion-channel currents. The proxy point follows from a definition: an approximation needs a well-defined target and an error bound. The paper's defences of IIT (the multi-dimensional measure, the "proto-consciousness" panpsychism) are revisions of the theory, not readings of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-529.md) | A state is shown to be a representation by adaptation for transmitting information efficiently, near the optimal trade-off of rate, distortion and coder complexity under a teleofunctionally fixed distortion measure, rather than by correlation or mutual information alone, which nearly any causal link supplies and which cannot increase along a processing chain | Martínez (2025), [LIT-149](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-149.md), read in [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md): a position paper with no new theorem or data. Its sharpest point is a standard result: by the data-processing inequality, mutual information about a car/no-car decision can only fall from retina to IT, so a mutual-information criterion would place the decision at the earliest stage; explicitness is better read as ease of decoding. The rest is a proposal supported by selected examples. Complexity has no operational measure, teleofunctions are needed to fix the distortion measure or every system is efficient for some loss, and misrepresentation and engineered systems are not addressed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md) | Whatever redundancy measure a partial information decomposition uses, provided its atoms satisfy the consistency equation, the average number of single sources an atom can be read from is Σᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y)/I(X;Y) and the average number of sources it cannot do without is Σⱼ I(Xⱼ;Y\|X₋ⱼ)/I(X;Y); so the redundancy–synergy index equals (r̄ − 1)·I(X;Y), and for three or more sources it counts a k-way redundancy k − 1 times but synergy once | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md), read in full in [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md), with the combinatorial proofs of Props. 1–4 and 6 checked by hand. The averages need only the consistency equation and I(X;Y) > 0; reading them as average degrees, and the bounds of Appendix B, need non-negative atoms. Corollary 5 overstates Prop. 6 (⇔ for ⇐). The network results are on tiny quantised models evaluated on their own training sets, and are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-581](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-581.md) v2 | Two exactly consistent descriptions of one system, at different scales and with equal past–future mutual information, can differ in how that information divides between redundancy and synergy; in small generated Boolean networks under the Williams–Beer redundancy measure the coarser scale was more synergy-biased in every random stochastic system, by at most about 0.07, and the direction mostly reversed for redundancy-biased deterministic ones | Varley & Hoel (2022), [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), read in [NOTE-020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-020.md). Expanding a 3-node macroscale TPM into 4- and 5-node equivalence-class microscales holds mutual information fixed with zero inconsistency, so any change in the PID's synergy bias B_syn is a change of type, not of amount. In 200 \|Gaussian\| TPMs the macroscale gained B_syn by about 0.005–0.07; in 185 near-deterministic ones most with macro B_syn < 0.5 lost it. One redundancy function, no robustness check, tiny constructed systems. The "unifying theory" of the title is a framing: the EI section re-describes a known decomposition and adds no result. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | The quantum fidelity tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) is exactly the classical Bhattacharyya overlap of the two states' outcome distributions minimized over all measurements, and the minimum is attained by a projective measurement whose eigenvalues are square roots of likelihood ratios | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-599](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-599.md) | In trained neural-network weights stored as BF16 or FP32, nearly all the redundancy a lossless coder can remove lies in the floating-point exponent, which occupies about 40 of its 256 values and compresses to about a third under single-symbol Huffman coding, while sign and mantissa are near-incompressible; the redundancy belongs to the number format, not to the learned function | Hershcovitch et al. (2024), ZipNN, [LIT-268](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md), read in full in [NOTE-241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-241.md). Fifteen models broken down by byte group (Table II), with the exponent skew shown on four (Fig. 2) from 1 GB middle slices. A parameter shuffle changes Zstd's exponent compression by at most 0.05%, so the gain is order-0. The paper never computes an entropy. Its explanation of the skew is partly wrong as stated, and its remark that the redundancy shows overparametrization unused does not follow from what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-602](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-602.md) | An ergodic source's entropy is the least average rate at which it can be encoded, a noisy channel has a capacity below which any rate can be sent with arbitrarily small error and above which the equivocation cannot fall below the excess, and a source can be reproduced at a given fidelity over a channel exactly when its rate for that fidelity does not exceed the capacity; Shannon rests the justification of entropy on these theorems, not on the axioms that single out −Σ p log p | Shannon (1948), [LIT-764](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-764.md), read in [NOTE-591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-591.md): Parts I–II closely, Parts III–V and the later appendices skimmed for their theorem statements. The noisy-channel achievability proof is a random-coding sketch at the typical-set level, not a full ε–δ argument, and the strong converse is not proved; the theorems themselves were later made rigorous. Shannon says the uniqueness theorem for H is "in no way necessary" to the theory. The theorems assume ergodic, finite-state sources and channels and say nothing about meaning. | Active |
| [THEORY-617](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-617.md) | In additive Gaussian noise independent of an input of finite power whose law does not depend on the signal-to-noise ratio, the derivative of mutual information with respect to that ratio is half the minimum mean-square error of the optimal noncausal estimator, so mutual information is accumulated estimation error over SNR; in continuous time the causal filtering error equals the noncausal error averaged over SNR, and the identity fails with feedback | Guo, Shamai & Verdú (2004), [LIT-058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-058.md), read in full in [NOTE-086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-086.md). Proved five ways for every finite-power input, in scalar, vector, discrete-time and continuous-time forms. It concerns the optimal, conditional-mean estimator; carrying it to a trained diffusion model's learned denoiser needs the mismatched version, which is later work. Theorems 3, 4 and 11 are stated without proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-641](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-641.md) v2 | Under a well-specified, identifiable parametric Markov model of the target given the joint past, with ergodic lagged states, transfer entropy is the limit of the normalised log-likelihood ratio for the null of no dependence on the source's past, so it is Granger-sense predictive improvement; for finite-state chains the plug-in estimator is exactly that statistic, and under the null and the usual regularity it is asymptotically χ² with the difference in parameter counts as degrees of freedom | Barnett & Bossomaier (2012), [LIT-048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-048.md), read in full in [NOTE-053](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-053.md). The consistency result is a one-line consequence of Props. 1–2, and Prop. 2 is argued informally. The χ² null is imported from Wald (1943), whose regularity conditions are not checked. The non-central χ² for T > 0 is at best a local-alternative approximation. The finite-state identity and the Gaussian equivalence (half the Granger statistic) are exact. | Active |
| [THEORY-668](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-668.md) | When the encoder is restricted to prunings of one fixed hierarchy of nested partitions, any non-negatively weighted sum of relevant information, irrelevant information and compression decomposes into per-node terms, so a bottom-up recursion finds the unique optimal tree with fewest leaves exactly in linear time, while greedy top-down splitting can miss information lying below a level that carries none; penalising irrelevant information only prunes the information-bottleneck tree | Larsson, Maity & Tsiotras (2022), [LIT-868](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-868.md), read in full in [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md), every proof followed step by step. The decomposition is the chain rule for refinements, and the recursion is the classic bottom-up pruning of a fixed tree. [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) declined a THEORY as exact but narrow; it is filed because the reading supports it as stated and its greedy-failure point bears on how hierarchy is measured. The hierarchy is given, not found, and the evaluation is one image. | Active |
| [THEORY-676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-676.md) | Dewar's information-theoretic derivation of maximum entropy production does not reach the far-from-equilibrium regime where the principle is applied: the 2003 route needs a mean-field step and an unargued assumption about path counts, the 2005 route's orthogonality condition, which yields both maximum and minimum dissipation, holds only with linear constitutive relations, and the 2003 self-organized-criticality corollary is an artefact of a quadratic expansion | Grinstein & Linsker (2007), [LIT-525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-525.md), read in [NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md), against Dewar (2003), [LIT-521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-521.md), read in [NOTE-426](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-426.md). The self-organized-criticality point was checked against Dewar 2003 and is correct. The linearity point concerns Dewar 2005, which the record could not read; it is held on the Comment's account of its equations and on an exactly solvable spin chain, re-derived. The Comment removes one derivation and one application. It does not say MEP is false, and it says the existence of far-from-equilibrium extremal principles "has not been settled". | Active |
| [THEORY-695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-695.md) | Two quantum states can be broadcast if and only if they commute, and cloned if and only if they are identical or orthogonal; the theorem is proved for invertible density operators and marks a line within quantum theory, not a witness of nonclassicality | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), §4.3, read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md), from the Barnum–Caves–Fuchs–Jozsa–Schumacher manuscript. Fidelity cannot decrease under partial trace or under the broadcasting map, so broadcasting forces equality conditions that make ρ0 commute with the optimal-fidelity operator. Proved for invertible ρ0, ρ1 only. Spekkens' epistricted classical theories ([LIT-007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md)) reproduce no-broadcasting, so the theorem states where broadcastability ends inside quantum theory and does not by itself certify nonclassicality. | Active |
| [THEORY-700](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-700.md) | For jointly Gaussian stationary processes, Granger causality in Geweke's generalized-variance form is exactly twice the transfer entropy, conditional and multivariate, at the regressions' lags, because least-squares residual covariance is the partial covariance and a Gaussian's conditional entropy is half its log-determinant plus a constant | Barnett, Barrett & Seth (2009), [LIT-1171](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1171.md), read in full in [NOTE-934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-934.md). F_{Y→X\|Z} = 2T_{Y→X\|Z}, exactly, for population quantities. The proof is two identities and was checked. Sample agreement depends on the entropy estimator. Both quantities are predictive; the authors keep them apart from physical causation. | Active |
| [THEORY-701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-701.md) | Transfer entropy from J to I is the Kullback entropy of assuming that I's next state, given its last k states, does not depend on J's last l states, so it is zero exactly when J's past leaves I's transition law unchanged; unlike time-delayed mutual information it is directional and zero for static correlation, and it removes a common input only when that input is conditioned on | Schreiber (2000), [LIT-1177](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1177.md), read in full in [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md). The definition and its zero condition are exact. The comparison with delayed mutual information rests on two coupled-map lattices built with a known direction. The continuum-limit claim is asserted. The Letter's tent-map coefficient appears to be twice what Eq. 4 gives. | Active |
| [THEORY-702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-702.md) | Transfer entropy is the average of a local transfer entropy, the log ratio at each observation of the destination's next-state probability with and without the source given the destination's past, which can be negative where the source misleads; the destination history must be long for it to exclude self-influence routed through the source; and conditioning also on the destination's other causal parents (complete) can differ sharply from conditioning on its past alone (apparent), as in elementary cellular automata, where long-history local transfer entropy picks out gliders and domain walls | Lizier, Prokopenko & Zomaya (2008), [LIT-1175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1175.md), read in full in [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md). The local decomposition is an identity; the claims about k and about particles rest on elementary CAs judged by eye. Three worked local values and rule 18's XOR structure were checked. | Active |
| [THEORY-705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-705.md) v2 | For a target and two sources with finite alphabets, if unique information is to depend only on the two source–target pair marginals, then the minimum of the conditional mutual information over all joints with those marginals is an upper bound on every non-negative decomposition's unique information, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds; this unique information vanishes exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient, and the measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate partial-information axioms and the identity property, and do not extend to three sources on the partial-information lattice | Bertschinger et al. (2014), [LIT-1162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1162.md), read in full in [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md). The bounds, the Blackwell characterisation and the properties are proved. The motivating property is argued, not derived. Example 30 and the Table 1 rows reproduce, except two entries that conflict with the paper's own Proposition 18. Under this measure, the record's transfer-entropy examples split exactly as under I_min. | Active |
| [THEORY-706](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-706.md) | Any redundancy function defined on the lattice of antichains of sources, ordered so that a collection precedes another when every source of the latter contains one of the former, has a Möbius inverse that decomposes the information a set of sources gives about a target into partial-information atoms summing to every subset's mutual information; for the I_min redundancy, the expected minimum specific information over sources, every atom is nonnegative, and interaction information is a signed mixture of atoms, synergy minus redundancy for three variables | Williams & Beer (2010), [LIT-1172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1172.md), read in full in [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md). The lattice, the inversion and the nonnegativity proofs are exact and were followed; the lattice sizes and the 3-parity and three-copies cases were checked. What is not shown is that I_min measures shared information: it gives two independent copied bits 1 bit of redundancy (Harder, Salge and Polani). | Active |
| [THEORY-707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md) | Transfer entropy is not a measure of information flow, if flow means information in the target attributable solely to the source's past: as a conditional mutual information it equals the source's unique information plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a full bit to a source that carries none alone (Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}) and report zero from each of two sources that jointly fix the target (Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1}); conditioning on further series, as causation entropy does, has the same fault | James, Barnett & Crutchfield (2016), [LIT-1165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1165.md), read in full in [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md). Both examples are exact and were recomputed. The decomposition holds for any PID satisfying the consistency equations. The conclusion is relative to the authors' definition of flow; transfer entropy as predictive improvement is untouched. The claims about directed information, interventional flow and Gaussian systems are cited or conjectured. | Active |
| [THEORY-708](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-708.md) v2 | The I_min redundancy credits two independent sources with shared information whenever each reduces surprise about the same target outcomes, so it gives two independent bits copied into the target 1 bit of redundancy; a bivariate redundancy built from reverse information projections, each source's information less what is lost when its posteriors are replaced by mixtures of the other's, satisfies symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity and the identity property, gives a nonnegative decomposition, and agrees with I_min on XOR, AND and their compositions but can reverse the state-independent/state-dependent split of a transfer entropy | Harder, Salge & Polani (2013), [LIT-1168](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1168.md), read in full in [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md). The counterexample, the axioms and the nonnegativity proof are exact; every Table I value and both transfer-entropy examples were recomputed. The identity axiom and "mechanistic redundancy" are positions, not results, and the measure is bivariate only. | Active |
| [THEORY-709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-709.md) | Mutual information between continuous variables can be estimated from k-nearest-neighbour statistics, with the joint k-th-neighbour distance in the maximum norm fixing the scale at which marginal neighbours are counted, so that the biases of the three entropy estimates largely cancel; the one approximation is a locally constant density, the systematic error scales with k/N, and exactness for independent variables is observed in every tested case but not proved | Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger (2004), [LIT-1163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1163.md), read in [NOTE-938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-938.md) (formal sections in full, numerics at lower resolution). The estimators are derived up to one approximation and one neglected correction; the rest is numerical. Checked by simulation on correlated Gaussians. | Active |
| [THEORY-710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-710.md) | In a finite causal Bayesian network, a set of nodes is causally independent of another, imposing a third, for every choice of mechanisms exactly when every directed path between them passes through the third; information flow, conditional mutual information computed from interventional instead of observational distributions, vanishes under causal independence, and it can differ from transfer entropy and conditional mutual information in either direction | Ay & Polani (2008), [LIT-1174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1174.md), read in full in [NOTE-946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-946.md) from the 2006 preprint. Theorem 2 and Prop. 3 are proved; Examples 3–6 were recomputed. Example 6's one bit holds at k = 1 and fails for k ≥ 2 as stated. The measure needs the mechanisms, and estimation and identification are not addressed. | Active |
| [THEORY-711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-711.md) | Directed information from an input sequence to an output sequence, the sum over time of the information the inputs up to now carry about the current output given the past outputs, is at most their mutual information and equal to it when the channel is used without feedback; in a causal system it bounds what the output reveals about the source, so feedback cannot raise a memoryless channel's capacity; and the usual definition of a memoryless channel holds only without feedback | Massey (1990), [LIT-1166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1166.md), read in full in [NOTE-939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-939.md) from the author's preprint. Three short theorems, all checked; the feedback inequality also checked numerically. "Causal" is Massey's factorization condition, not intervention. That directed information is full-history transfer entropy plus instantaneous terms is the record's derivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md) v2 | Under any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations, a transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of the source's past about the target's next state plus the synergy of source and target pasts, which Williams and Beer call state-independent and state-dependent transfer; time-delayed mutual information is the unique part plus redundancy; with the I_min redundancy the state-independent part alone suffices for perfect open-loop control, and a two-source transfer entropy splits into unique, redundant and synergistic transfer | Williams & Beer (2011), [LIT-1176](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1176.md), an arXiv preprint, read in full in [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md). The two-term split is an identity from the consistency equations; the sizes of the terms, the control theorem and the multivariate split use I_min, which the record has not read argued for. The one-parameter family and the three corners of the two-source family were recomputed. The text mislabels the synergistic corner. | Active |
| [THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md) | No redundancy measure on the Williams–Beer partial-information lattice can satisfy symmetry, self-redundancy, monotonicity, the identity axiom and non-negative atoms once there are three sources: for two independent bits, their XOR and a target that copies all three, identity forces three one-bit atoms under a two-bit total, so one atom is at most −1 bit, and a multivariate decomposition that keeps identity must give up non-negativity or the lattice | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich & Jost (2014), [LIT-1202](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), read in full in [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md). A proved impossibility, checked by hand and by script. It also uses invariance of redundancy under relabelling the target, which is not stated as an axiom. I_min escapes it by failing identity, Ince's I_ccs by accepting the −1-bit atom. | Active |
| [THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md) | Redundancy among any number of sources can be measured as the expected local co-information over only those events where every source, the joint source and the overlap change the target's surprisal in the same direction, under the maximum-entropy joint that preserves the source–target and joint-source marginals; this keeps symmetry, self-redundancy, subset equality and identity for independent sources, and gives up Harder et al.'s identity, monotonicity and non-negative atoms, which then read as local misinformation and mechanistic redundancy | Ince (2017), [LIT-1201](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1201.md), read in [NOTE-968](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-968.md). The definition and the four kept properties are exact, and every discrete example reproduces. That the dropped properties ought to be dropped, and that unique information depends on the source–source marginal, are argued, not proved. Proposed until one of those is settled. It meets Rauh et al.'s −1-bit bound exactly on XORCOPY. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-715](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-715.md) | The information about a target carried by the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources is a redundancy defined for any number of sources that is nonnegative, target-monotone and no larger than I_min, and is a lower bound on any reasonable redundancy; but it counts only deterministic shared structure, so it is zero whenever the sources' joint distribution has full support, fails the identity property and continuity, and gives negative synergy already for two sources | Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison & Crutchfield (2014), [LIT-1203](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1203.md), read in full in [NOTE-967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md). The lemmas are short and exact, and every example was recomputed, with Harder, Salge and Polani's copy family and a three-source copy added. It is the record's one redundancy defined for n > 2, and it does not have the identity property there or for n = 2. | Active |
| [THEORY-716](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-716.md) | Synergy can be measured as the whole minus the union of its parts, the union information being the least information the sources could jointly carry about the target with every source–target marginal held fixed; this synergy lies between WholeMinusSum and Williams and Beer's S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique information as synergy, and for two sources it is Bertschinger et al.'s synergy, so independent sources can share information about a target, as the authors' last version concedes against their first | Griffith & Koch (2014), [LIT-1204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1204.md), read in full in [NOTE-966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md), v6 with v1–v2 checked. The definitions, the criticisms of S_max, WMS and ΔI, and the properties proved in Appendix C are exact, and every Table 1 value for two predictors was recomputed. The identification with Bertschinger et al.'s CI for two sources is the record's derivation. Monotonicity is claimed without proof, and the S_max bound's proof has a step the reading could not reconstruct. | Active |
| [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | For experiments with finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, being at least as informative in every decision problem is the same as being reproducible from the other by a Markov matrix | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof. With n states and finite outcome sets, write experiments as n × N Markov matrices P and Q. Every risk vector Q attains in every decision problem is attainable with P exactly when Q = PM for some Markov matrix M. The arbitrary-outcome extension is [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), still Proposed. A qualitative order: most pairs are incomparable, and it says nothing about how far apart they are. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md) | For a stable linear Gaussian VAR(p), a linear coarse-graining is exactly dynamically independent iff its row space is invariant under the transpose of every lag matrix, so for p ≥ 2 almost no parameter set has one at any scale, while for p = 1 they are the transpose's invariant subspaces, which exist on open sets but not generically at every scale | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): the VAR form (3.26) of exact dynamical independence, with the genericity count of §3.3 made a proof for VAR order p ≥ 2 and corrected for p = 1. Linear coarse-grainings Y = LX of a stable VAR with non-degenerate Gaussian innovations only. It says nothing about near-independence, about the multimodality of the dynamical-dependence cost, or about nonlinear maps. | Active |
